title: Resistance at fixed voltage
hook: Change resistance and predict resistor power.
misconception: resistor power doubles when resistance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply P = V²/R to compare resistor power when resistance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ohmic resistor with fixed voltage magnitude, P = V²/R. When resistance doubles, resistor power becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P = V²/R; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ohmic resistor with fixed voltage magnitude, with a nonzero initial result. If resistance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on resistor power?
recall.why: Apply P = V²/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
